packet.background: The exact September CPI summary and its embedded main-category monthly/annual table, released 14 October, are retained. Headline and core, monthly seasonally adjusted changes and annual unadjusted changes must remain distinct. The capture is raw background, not an admitted chart dataset.
comparison_plan: Compare October and September on the same metric, period, unit and seasonal-adjustment basis.
Preserve raw index levels separately from monthly and annual percentage changes; retain actual revisions rather than overwriting the September capture.
Use admitted component evidence for attribution; do not assume the prior energy movement persists or infer a market surprise without a separately admitted expectation.
missing_inputs: Actual October CPI release, exact table edition and known-at at T0
Table/header/footnote admission and lawful chart transformation before any chart is created
No filled October values, imputed components or invented expectations
packet.official_attribution: Attribute actual released facts naturally to the named official issuer; attributed reporting and market reaction require their own exact sources and clocks.

prior_fact_spans.exact_source_span:
The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.6 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in 
September after rising 0.4 percent in August, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Over the last 12 
months, the all items index increased 3.7 percent before seasonal adjustment.
prior_fact_spans.metric: Headline monthly SA and annual NSA percent

prior_fact_spans.exact_source_span:
The index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3 percent in September, as it did in August. Indexes that increased 
over the month include recreation, used cars and trucks, education, airline fares, medical care, and apparel. Conversely, 
the index for communication was among the small number of major indexes that decreased in September.

The all items less food and energy index rose 2.6 percent over the year, 
following a 2.4-percent increase over the 12 months ending August.

Admit only the bounded new facts; native Light preparation then same MAX writing/final rendered review and sole coordinator. This packet allocates no operation, fetch budget or publication.

update_frames: If headline and core diverge, lead with the evidenced component mechanism rather than treating one as the whole inflation picture.
If annual and monthly directions diverge, explain their distinct comparison periods using actual admitted figures.
Use a broadening/narrowing frame only after comparable components support it; no automatic extrapolation of September gasoline movement.
watchpoints: Separate headline/core and monthly SA/annual NSA; do not compare rates with different bases.
Check actual energy, shelter and food contributions or source explanation; a component rate alone is not a weighted contribution.
A lower annual rate can reflect base effects; test against actual monthly and component evidence before explaining causality.
Preserve September vintage if the October release revises comparable seasonal figures; no surprise claim without admitted expectation.
